A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same I2I-RFR research work, including all 38 pages and Appendices A-G. Pages 2-38 have identical text and rendered content; page 1 differs only in its arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original image and video translation experiments in Section 4, with runtime measurements, ablations, and additional qualitative applications in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original quantitative experiments, runtime measurements, ablations, and qualitative results in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1-2 retain identical input concatenation, target prediction, t-reweighted loss, Beta sampling, and Euler inference procedures. The task-specific adaptations in Appendix F are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is identical, including super-resolution, deblurring, low-light and underwater enhancement, video restoration, and Appendix F's inpainting, colorization, and label-to-image applications.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every corresponding experiment, including the task-specific backbones, U-Net and Palette comparisons, and Appendix D's loss, DDPM, bridge-path, and guidance variants.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A-D and F retain the same datasets and splits, preprocessing, metrics, training settings, checkpoint selection, and inference procedures, including the default three Euler steps and 15-step inpainting setting.

E4.justification: The sampling, prediction-parameterization, time-embedding, inference-depth, bridge-path, loss, and guidance studies are identical. Cross-dataset evaluations and qualitative case studies are also retained without revision.

E5.justification: Both versions specify a fixed evaluation seed and one generated sample per input. Runtime averaging over up to 100 samples is unchanged, and neither version adds repeated-run uncertainty estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results, rankings, plotted trends, and qualitative outputs are unchanged. For example, Table 3 reports LEDNet + I2I-RFR at PSNR 27.42, SSIM 0.874, and LPIPS 0.138 in both versions; appendix results also match.

T1.justification: The interpolation definitions, induced-velocity derivation, equivalence to the reweighted regression objective, time-reversal reasoning, and Beta-sampling weighting argument are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about minimally modifying regression backbones, enabling few-step continuous-time refinement, and improving perceptual quality across image and video tasks.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including perception-distortion trade-offs, backbone-dependent outcomes, explanations for parameterization and guidance effects, and the qualification that Beta sampling is not universally optimal.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information is identical, including optimization settings, hardware, normalization, checkpoint selection, baseline sampling schedules, and task-specific instructions in Appendices A, C, D, and F.

R1.justification: Section 2, subsequent research-positioning discussions, and all 57 references are unchanged. No cited work or relationship to prior methods is added or removed.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 20 Mar 2026 to v2 dated 31 Aug 2026. Manuscript prose, authors, headings, terminology, and section organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, and manuscript layout are unchanged. The first-page arXiv stamp changes font and position; in v2 it intrudes into the Introduction section number and the left edge of the opening paragraph.

improvement.justification: Scientific content and supporting evidence, including all appendices, are unchanged. The only quality difference is a small presentation deterioration: v2's repositioned arXiv stamp overlaps the Introduction section number and beginnings of several lines, slightly reducing first-page readability.
